steps.title: Definition
steps.body: Inference means using evidence from the text AND your own reasoning to work out meanings that are NOT directly stated. You "read between the lines."

steps.title: PEE Structure
steps.body: P oint - State your inference E vidence - Quote from the text E xplain - Show how the evidence proves your point

steps.title: Inference Exam Strategy
steps.body: Always use the PEE structure - Point, Evidence, Explanation. Your point should state the inferred meaning clearly, your evidence must be a short quotation, and your explanation must show HOW the evidence leads to your inference. For AQA Paper 1 Q2 and Paper 2 Q3, spend 10-12 minutes. Examiners reward specific, well-supported inferences over vague guesses. Always ask yourself: "What does this word/phrase suggest, and how do I know?"

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always support inferences with quotations Use PEE structure for clear, structured answers Focus on words with strong connotations Be specific - avoid vague emotional words Consider the wider context, not just isolated words Trust your instincts but verify with evidence
